name: issue_786_tou_precondition_banks_then_coasts
description: A cost_period schedule tagged 'high' from 16:15-21:00. Before the schedule's lead-time window opens, the home holds its normal comfort band (ceiling=comfort_cool=76F, cool mode). Once the window opens (fallback lead time 45min, Issue #797's configurable default, since no thermal model observations exist -> opens 15:30), the automation engine banks toward the OPPOSITE comfort-band edge (comfort_heat=68F) instead -- no user-authored temperature field anywhere drove this, it is derived automatically from the existing comfort band. Once the schedule's own start time (16:15) is reached, pre-conditioning stops being called and the comfort-edge selector (Issue #1066, Design D nearest-edge arming) resumes. In this scenario indoor stays at 76F throughout (the scenario never feeds the banked temperature back), so the selector still sees the ceiling edge and the plain comfort_cool=76F ceiling is armed -- that is why the assertion holds. In a real home the bank would have drawn indoor down toward the 68F floor edge: the selector would then arm heat at the floor, and flip back to cool only once indoor climbs to ceiling minus the arming margin; a bank overshoot below the floor is an ordinary floor breach. Coast itself still needs no new suppression code, since _apply_comfort_band() issues a single-setpoint THRESHOLD command a real thermostat only acts on when indoor crosses it, not a proactive drive-to-target.
source: Issue #786 design/implementation session; fallback lead time updated to the Issue #797 default (45min, was 120min) and made configurable
notes: (a) Scenario effectiveness: deleting coordinator._resolve_tou_schedule_state()/_apply_tou_schedule()'s call sites (or automation.py's apply_tou_precondition()) causes the 15:30 assertion (tou_precondition_applied, target=68.0) to FAIL -- no such event would ever fire, reproducing 'the TOU feature silently does nothing' exactly.

(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/scheduler-spec.md documents this exact resolve-then-act sequence and the coast-is-free finding; this scenario checks the pre-bank band and the bank itself against production. Honest limit (Issue #1066 review): it does NOT guard post-bank coast behavior -- indoor is held at 76F for the whole scenario, so the 16:15 assertion only shows that with indoor at the ceiling the selector arms the ceiling; it says nothing about what the selector does with a house banked toward the floor.

(c) Occupant experience: without this feature, the home runs the AC at its normal comfort_cool ceiling straight through a scheduled high-cost window (e.g. 4:15-9:00pm peak electricity rates), paying peak-rate cost with no cost-aware behavior. With it, the home banks extra coolness to comfort_heat before the window starts and coasts on that banked cool air through the expensive hours -- lower cost, and the occupant configured zero new temperature settings to get it; the system derived the banking target from settings they already had (comfort_heat) and the home's own learned response rate.

events.note: Hot afternoon. Indoor already at the normal comfort ceiling.

Before the TOU lead window opens (16:15 - 45min fallback lead = 15:30, since no thermal model observations exist yet and no custom default_tou_lead_minutes is configured in this scenario). Normal comfort band arms: ceiling=comfort_cool=76F, cool mode.

Next 30-min cycle -- now sits exactly at the lead window's open instant (15:30). TOU pre-conditioning fires: banks to comfort_heat=68F (the OPPOSITE edge from the normal ceiling), cool mode, ahead of the 16:15 high-cost window. No temperature field was configured for this -- 68F is the home's own existing comfort_heat value.

Schedule's own start time reached -- TOU phase reverts to NONE (pre-conditioning stops being called this cycle) and the comfort-edge selector resumes. Indoor is still 76F in this scenario (it is never fed back from the bank), so the selector arms the ceiling edge (comfort_cool=76F). A real banked house sitting near the 68F floor would instead be armed heat at the floor until it rises to ceiling minus the arming margin.

assertions.reason: Normal 30-min classification cycle runs as always.
Before the TOU lead window opens, the plain comfort_cool ceiling (76F) is armed -- no TOU influence yet.

The lead window has opened -- production banks to comfort_heat=68F (cool mode) ahead of the 16:15 high-cost window, derived automatically from the existing comfort_heat config value and the home's own thermal response rate (default 45-minute fallback lead time here, since no observations exist and no custom default_tou_lead_minutes is configured).

Schedule start reached -- pre-conditioning stops firing and the comfort-edge selector resumes; with indoor still at the 76F ceiling edge (this scenario never feeds the banked temperature back) the ceiling (76F) is armed. This asserts only that the selector resumes arming the ceiling edge when indoor is there; it does NOT cover post-bank coast with a house banked toward the floor. No separate coast-phase suppression code exists: the single-setpoint threshold command _apply_comfort_band() issues is idle while indoor sits inside the band.

verdict.summary: TOU pre-conditioning banks to the comfort-band floor ahead of a scheduled high-cost window using zero user-authored temperature settings, then hands control back to the comfort-edge selector once the window starts, with zero new suppression code (post-bank coast with a genuinely banked house is not exercised by this scenario).
verdict.observed_behavior: Normal comfort_cool ceiling (76F) held before the lead window opens -> banks to comfort_heat (68F) once the default 45-minute fallback lead window opens ahead of the 16:15 schedule -> the selector resumes at the schedule's own start time and, with indoor still at the ceiling edge in this scenario, arms the comfort_cool ceiling (76F), with no dedicated coast-phase code involved.
verdict.expected_behavior: The occupant pays less to run AC during a scheduled expensive electricity window by having the home pre-cool using thermal mass it already has, using only settings (comfort_heat) and behavior (learned thermal rate) the system already knew about -- no new temperature configuration required for this feature to work.
